what: Our arm against upstream's own bf16 step, per section, with an attribution for every outlier. A faithful bf16 reproduction should read near 1.0x; this spans 0.010x to 6.861x.
why: The model-scope arm is STITCHED from five legs produced by five harnesses in four rows (see MODEL_withtrunk_n384.json `arms`), each driven from its own boundary. D186 proved the pairformer leg is cross-frame. This table asks the same of every other leg and records what is explained and what is not.
read_this_way: a ratio near 1.0 is the signature of reproducing upstream's arithmetic. Far ABOVE 1.0 means we are worse; far BELOW means we are not doing what they do -- which can be deliberate (higher precision) and is still a divergence from 'reproduce their step'.

sections.why: 2.019x on 43.622 % of the mass. With the trunk reframed by D186 this is the campaign's biggest unexplained accuracy gap. D56 is live on this arm and D172 resolved its old 8.1943 as a pre-D56 reading; the residual 2.019x has no owner.

D186: our arm is capture-driven and this denominator is a full-model run. Frame-matched at c64 the same tensors read 0.9565x. The 6.861x is the frame.
